counterexample: Take D = Q with its usual ordered-field structure. Its characteristic is zero and the canonical map g: Z → Q is injective, but it is not onto Q (for example, 1/2 is not in its image).
assessment_summary: 0001: Correct; the cited standard ordered-ring property may be applied to positive integer multiples of 1_D. 0002: Correct; in an ordered integral domain, 1_D>0 and every positive integer multiple n·1_D is positive. 0003: No assertion; blank formatting line. 0004: Correct; this introduces the consequence of the preceding positivity statement. 0005: Correct; if Char D=p>0, then p·1_D=0_D, contradicting step 0002. 0006: No assertion; blank formatting line. 0007: Correct; this introduces the next consequence. 0008: Correct; a ring's characteristic is either zero or a positive integer, and step 0005 excludes every positive value. 0009: No assertion; blank formatting line. 0010: Correct; the canonical unital ring homomorphism g:Z→D has trivial kernel when Char D=0, hence is injective and therefore a ring monomorphism into D. 0011: No assertion; blank formatting line. 0012: Correct, with m,p implicitly integers; m
